title: Mara and the Tryouts
premise: Mirabel Joubert, nonbinary statistician for the Hollow Creek Ravens, has spent two years quietly proving the school's championship games are rigged by an old booster pact — and telling no one, because 'fine' is easier. When the ghost of Ada Voss, a player who died in 1968 before her own rigged final, starts leaving notes in ink that appears only to Mirabel, they discover the rigging is a bargain: the school trades one forgotten student's memory per championship win. To break it, Mirabel must lead the team — from the bench, through numbers — to win a championship that matters honestly, while racing Ada's fading memory and their own erasure. In the end, Mirabel forfeits the rigged title publicly, wins the real one in overtime, and chooses to remember Ada even as the town forgets, sealing the pact shut with a name spoken aloud.
about_author: Mirabel Vasquez is a former high-school scorekeeper from the Gulf Coast who writes stories about kids who see the machinery behind the magic. They live with three cats and an unhealthy collection of vintage scorebooks.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. During a blowout win, Mirabel logs statistically impossible plays and quietly adds them to a hidden folder of evidence. Establishes their role as observer, their crush on captain Dee Okafor, and the mantra: everything is fine. Beat: controlled unease.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds a note in their locker — their full name, including the name only family uses — written in ink that shimmers violet and vanishes when photographed. No fingerprints, no explanation. Beat: first crack in 'fine.'

chapters.title: Ada Voss, 1968
chapters.summary: Researching in the library archive, Mirabel finds a trophy case photo of Ada Voss, star of the '68 team who died before the final. The handwriting on her preserved playbook matches the notes exactly. Beat: dread mixed with fascination.

chapters.title: Second Note
chapters.summary: A note predicts tomorrow's exact score before the game happens. It's right. Mirabel, terrified, almost throws it away — then pockets it instead. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: Dee Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Dee notices Mirabel distracted at practice and pushes; Mirabel deflects badly, hurting them both. POV shifts briefly to Dee, who worries Mirabel is pulling away. Beat: love vs. secrecy.

chapters.title: The Booster Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel sneaks into the locked booster room and finds fifty years of ledgers — every championship year paired with a student name struck through. Their own name is penciled in, not yet crossed out. Beat: cold horror.

chapters.title: Talk to Me, Ada
chapters.summary: Mirabel speaks aloud to the empty gym, asking what Ada wants. A note appears mid-air: 'They took my name. Help me take it back.' Beat: alliance formed.

chapters.title: Rules of Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Through exchanged notes, Mirabel learns the ghost can only write truths and only to someone who already suspects the truth. Ada tests Mirabel with riddles about the '68 game. Beat: wary partnership.

chapters.title: The First Forgetting
chapters.summary: A classmate, Sam, stops remembering Mirabel mid-conversation — small, chilling, deniable. Mirabel realizes the pact has started collecting on their name early. Beat: stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Title chapter: winter tryouts for the tournament roster. Coach Whitlock, under booster pressure, benches Mirabel's ally Priya and promotes a mediocre player whose parent donates heavily. Mirabel watches the rigging happen live. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: What Dee Knows
chapters.summary: Dee admits she's suspected fixed games since sophomore year but stayed silent to protect her scholarship. She and Mirabel nearly confess everything to each other — and don't. Beat: aching near-intimacy.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel cross-references the struck-through names: each belonged to a student who 'transferred away' or died young, remembered by no one. Ada Voss was the first entry. Beat: grief at scale.

chapters.title: Ada's Last Game
chapters.summary: Through a dream sequence, Mirabel experiences Ada's 1968 final — the fix, the crash on the icy road fleeing town, the promise she made to come back. Beat: empathy cemented.

chapters.title: Priya's Suspicion
chapters.summary: Priya catches Mirabel copying ledger pages and demands answers. Mirabel lies; Priya doesn't believe it but lets it go — for now. Beat: isolation deepens.

chapters.title: Midseason Collapse
chapters.summary: The Ravens lose ugly to a rival, exactly as the odds demanded. Dee plays brilliantly and it isn't enough. Mirabel must decide whether to tell the team the truth. Beat: despair.

chapters.title: Confession in the Equipment Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel tells Dee everything — ledgers, notes, Ada. Dee's reaction isn't disbelief; it's fear for Mirabel's name on the list. Beat: love declared sideways, through worry.

chapters.title: The Third Note Changes
chapters.summary: Ada's notes begin arriving incomplete, letters missing — her memory is degrading as the anniversary of her death approaches. Urgency spikes. Beat: ticking clock made visible.

chapters.title: Coach Whitlock's Bargain
chapters.summary: Whitlock privately offers Mirabel a college recommendation in exchange for 'keeping the stats clean.' Mirabel understands the coach is both victim and enforcer. Beat: moral complexity.

chapters.title: Sam Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Sam fully forgets Mirabel — greets them as a stranger. Mirabel, shaken, finds their own name half-struck in the ledger. Beat: lowest personal point so far.

chapters.title: Halfway: The Scorebook
chapters.summary: Mirabel discovers Ada's original 1968 scorebook hidden in the bleachers, its final page torn out. Whatever was recorded there could void the pact. Beat: hope rekindled.

chapters.title: What Was Torn Out
chapters.summary: Reconstruction attempt: Ada's note reveals the torn page held the honest final score of the '68 game — proof the championship was never legitimately won. Beat: the goal crystallizes.

chapters.title: Winning Ugly
chapters.summary: Quarterfinal: Mirabel feeds Dee play calls that exploit the riggers' predictable script, winning honestly within a dishonest system. First taste of agency. Beat: defiant joy.

chapters.title: Priya Joins
chapters.summary: Priya confronts Mirabel again; this time Mirabel tells the truth. Priya, a journalism student, starts building the exposé. Team of three becomes conspiracy of three. Beat: solidarity.

chapters.title: The Boosters Notice
chapters.summary: Someone searches Mirabel's locker; the ledger pages are gone. A new note appears — not from Ada — reading simply: 'Stop.' Beat: human antagonists surface.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Fifty years to the day. Ada's notes are nearly illegible. She asks Mirabel to finish what she couldn't: speak her full name where the whole town can hear. Beat: tender urgency.

chapters.title: Semifinal Sabotage
chapters.summary: The boosters rig the semifinal against the Ravens. Dee injures her ankle on a sabotaged court floor; the team loses by two. Beat: fury and heartbreak.

chapters.title: Dee's Choice
chapters.summary: Dee, told she can have her scholarship back if she stays quiet, refuses — publicly, spectacularly, at the booster dinner. She burns her bridge for the truth. Beat: love against duty, embodied.

chapters.title: Appeal
chapters.summary: Priya's article forces an emergency board hearing on whether the semifinal result stands. Mirabel testifies with statistics; the board wavers. Beat: fragile victory.

chapters.title: The Replay Is Granted
chapters.summary: The championship will be replayed in full — winner takes the real title. The boosters make one last offer to Mirabel: their name comes off the ledger if they throw it. Beat: temptation at maximum.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: Mirabel and Dee on the gym floor, trading fears and almost-kisses; Ada's final legible note arrives — 'Say it loud. Say it whole.' Beat: stillness before storm.

chapters.title: Championship, First Half
chapters.summary: Game POV, fast and kinetic. The rigged system fights back — bad calls, hostile crowd — and the Ravens trail by eleven at halftime. Beat: mounting pressure.

chapters.title: Halftime Speech
chapters.summary: Mirabel, the statistician who never speaks, addresses the team with the truth: the game is rigged, and winning anyway is the only revenge that counts. Beat: rallying cry.

chapters.title: Championship, Second Half
chapters.summary: The comeback: Priya's defense, Dee playing hurt, Mirabel's numbers turning chaos into a plan. Tie game, final possession. Beat: exhilaration.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.summary: Overtime possession, seconds left. Mirabel calls the play Ada ran in 1968 — the one erased from every record. Dee scores. The Ravens win honestly. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Say Her Name
chapters.summary: At the trophy ceremony, instead of accepting the old (rigged) title's retroactive recognition, Mirabel takes the microphone and speaks Ada Voss's full name to the entire gym. The lights flicker; the ink-pact shatters. Beat: climax.

chapters.title: What the Town Forgot
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the boosters' memories of the pact dissolve; records unseal; Ada's 1968 box score restores itself in the archive. But Ada herself is fading, finally free. Beat: bittersweet awe.

chapters.title: Last Note
chapters.summary: One final note appears in ordinary blue ballpoint — Ada, mortal-ink now: 'Thank you, Mirabel Joubert.' Then nothing, ever again. Beat: farewell.

chapters.title: Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Mirabel organizes a memorial plaque for Ada and the other struck-through students, restoring names to the record. Sam remembers Mirabel — gradually, imperfectly, enough. Beat: healing.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Mirabel's POV, echoing chapter one: same gym, same scorebook, but now the numbers are honest and so are they. Dee takes their hand. Everything is fine — actually, this time. Beat: earned peace.
